chapter: Leaving the band, Strayhorn and reflections
title: Strayhorn did not change the style; Take the A Train versus Toodle-oo
summary: Strayhorn added ideas but changed only the theme song; Greer prefers East St. Louis Toodle-oo.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So you remember that when he came, when Stravhorn came into the band, did the music change a lot after Stravhorn came or did it change a little bit?

Did we change our style? No. No, he just added things to it. We never changed our style. No, it was too big a gamble, we never changed our style. But we played a lot of Billy's ideas because fit right in with our band.
But we changed our style never, never. No. Him and Duke would collaborate on a lot of numbers but the style was right there. Billy fell right in, the style was right there.
Only thing Billy changed was our theme song, "Take the A Train."
Yeah, because the old one used to was "East St. Louis --

Two classics. You got a record of that? Oh, yes, that was a classic. When them cats heard that, they know we was coming through. I don't know, I couldn't fall in love with "A Train" because it was just ordinary. But that "East St. Louis Toodle-oo", we were saying something. That was that growl, that's thunder and lightning, man. I don't know, I really to this day don't know why we didn't keep that. That was one of the brilliant things he ever wrote. Bubber Miley named that. "East St. Louis Toodle-oo"
